sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is suffering confinement since 31/03/2024 and charge-sheet is likely to be filed soon, therefore, chance of tampering with the evidence/ witnesses is remote.

It is further submitted that applicant and prosecutrix share physical and emotional proximity with consent and prosecutrix left her matrimonial home (prosecutrix is married) on her own volition and both live together for some time in Delhi and Gurgaon without raising any alarm.
Now she is living with her husband at village Babakheda District Tikamgarh.
In fact, they entered into a wedlock but this aspect would not be pressed by the applicant to harass the prosecutrix.
He undertakes to abide by all the terms and conditions as imposed by this Court and would not be a source of embarrassment and harassment to the prosecutrix/ complainant in any manner.
4 . Learned counsel for the respondent/ State opposed the prayer and submitted that because of the nature of allegations, he suffered confinement.
However, he fairly submitted that the applicant does not bear any criminal record on the basis of case diary.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and considered the arguments advanced by them.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court intends to allow the present appeal and it is hereby directed that the appellant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.

(vii) The appellant would not be a source of embarrassment or harassment to the prosecutrix in any manner and shall not move in the vicinity of prosecutrix's village Mithun Rajak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6222875/
2 Babakheda District Tikamgarh and shall not try to contact her in person through electronic mode or through somebody else.

sentences.text: (viii) The appellant shall mark his presence on first and fifteenth day of every month before the concerned police station between 10:00 am. to 2:00 p.m. for next one year.
Appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
